findings.text: A mapping object distinguishes two address spaces with a boolean discriminator. When the discriminator is clear the object carries a normal virtual address and when set it carries an input output virtual address. Initializers and setters establish pointer and discriminator together. Equality compares discriminators first and then only the active pointer, null testing examines only the active pointer, set testing negates null, and clearing zeroes the whole object.

Advancing a mapping adds a byte displacement to whichever pointer is active while preserving the discriminator. An offset helper copies a source mapping by value and then advances the copy, leaving the original unchanged and giving value semantics for derived views.

Bulk helpers operate at a byte offset from the active base. Copy into the mapping, copy out of it, and fill each branch on the discriminator: the input output case uses input output aware helpers and the normal case uses regular memory helpers. Offset is applied to the base before the operation and a length controls the span.

Typed single value access dispatches on the discriminator and on value width. Widths of one, two and four bytes use dedicated input output accessors on the input output path and guarded single access loads or stores on the normal path. Eight byte handling has two build variants, one using dedicated sixty four bit input output accessors and one emulating with input output byte copy helpers. Field helpers add a member displacement within a structure type to a base displacement and infer member width from the member type.

Two callback types drive iteration. The kernel variant receives a kernel base plus progress and length plus opaque contexts passed through from the iterator. The user variant receives a user base with the same progress, length and context shape. Callbacks report unprocessed remainder and iteration converts remainder into consumed progress.

Single buffer and vector iteration share a consumption machine. Each step consumes a bounded piece, progress accumulates consumed bytes, a per segment skip advances, segment pointers move forward when a segment is exhausted, remaining segment count and total remaining count decrease, and iteration stops early when the callback leaves remainder. Zero length vector pieces are skipped without invoking the callback.

Block vector iteration maps one page at a time with a thread local mapping. Each callback piece is limited by remaining request length, remaining segment length after skip, and distance to the next page boundary. The mapping is released right after the callback, progress and skip advance by consumed bytes, fully consumed segments advance the pointer with skip reset, and any remainder ends the loop.

Folio queue iteration tracks a queue pointer plus slot index plus intra folio skip. A slot at the end follows to a next queue when present, including the case where the iterator was extended. Missing folios stop iteration. Otherwise it maps the folio at the skip, bounds the piece by remaining length and page boundary distance, invokes the callback, releases the mapping, advances progress and skip, moves to the next slot or next queue when folio size is reached, and stops on remainder.

Array backed iteration holds a read side critical section for the whole lookup loop. It derives a start from base plus offset, retries continuation entries, aborts on value entries or huge page entries with a warning, and processes each folio in page bounded pieces with temporary local mappings. On exit the iterator offset and remaining count are updated before the critical section is released.

Three dispatch helpers form the public iteration entry. They clamp requested length to remaining count and return zero when nothing remains. The full variant prefers single user buffer then user vector then block vector then kernel vector then folio queue then array, falling back to discard. The single context variant forwards with a null second context. The kernel only variant omits user cases and otherwise follows the same order with discard fallback.

Discard iteration consumes the requested length without invoking any callback and without touching segment state beyond decrementing remaining count. It serves as fallback for unrecognized iterator kinds and for kernel dispatch when no kernel kind matches.

The address bitmap interface in this configuration is non operational. Allocation always yields a null handle, release does nothing, and enumeration always reports operation not supported. A callback type is defined for enumeration consumers.

Protocol header helpers derive pointers from a socket buffer by adding stored header offsets to the head pointer. One helper yields the outer network header, one yields the inner network header for tunneled packets, and one reuses the transport header offset for encapsulated headers.

Length handling interprets the total length field in network order. Transport payload length subtracts network header length from total length. Total length retrieval falls back to buffer length minus network offset when the field is zero on segmented transmission control packets, otherwise it uses the field. Setting total length stores a network order value within maximum and zero when larger. Header length is transport offset minus network offset, network offset is network pointer minus data pointer, and segmentation state derives from shared info size and type flags.
IP_MAX_MTU denotes value 65535 as the upper bound for total datagram length.
Extension header length helpers compute byte sizes from a unit field. The generic option length adds one then scales by eight, while authentication length adds two then scales by four.

Device configuration holds many signed controls for forwarding, router advertisement handling, neighbor discovery, duplicate address detection, multicast behavior, temporary addresses and segment routing, with a small fast path group for receive and transmit, plus conditional router preference, route information, optimistic duplicate detection, multicast forwarding, segment authentication, quality of service and carrier handling fields. A nested stable secret pairs an initialized flag with an address, a separate small parameter structure carries only global disable and autoconfiguration flags, and a system control header pointer anchors runtime tuning.

Version six header helpers mirror version four placement: outer header from network offset, inner header from inner network offset, encapsulated header from transport offset. Transport length adds payload length to fixed header size then subtracts network header length.

Payload length retrieval uses the network order payload field unless it is zero on segmented transmission control packets, in which case it derives length from buffer length minus network offset and fixed header size. A convenience wrapper applies this to the outer header. Setting payload length stores a network order value within maximum and zero when larger.
IPV6_MAXPLEN denotes value 65535 as the upper bound for payload length.

Per packet control storage records incoming interface, router alert value, destination and source routing offsets, last option and next header offsets, flags, fragment size limit and segment routing offset, with an extra destination header offset present only when mobility support is enabled. Flag bits distinguish transformed, forwarded, rerouted, router alert, fragmented, hop by hop, layer three slave, jumbogram, segment routing, multipath and multicast route states.

Control flag values are IP6SKB_XFRM_TRANSFORMED one, IP6SKB_FORWARDED two, IP6SKB_REROUTED four, IP6SKB_ROUTERALERT eight, IP6SKB_FRAGMENTED sixteen, IP6SKB_HOPBYHOP thirty two, IP6SKB_L3SLAVE sixty four, IP6SKB_JUMBOGRAM one hundred twenty eight, IP6SKB_SEG6 two hundred fifty six, IP6SKB_MULTIPATH one thousand twenty four, IP6SKB_MCROUTE two thousand forty eight.

Layer three master device testing has two build variants: one tests the slave flag bit and the other always reports false. Incoming interface selection returns the socket buffer interface when slave is indicated and stored control interface otherwise, while slave device index returns stored interface only when slave is indicated and zero otherwise. Jumbogram testing checks its flag bit, and a buffer control accessor reinterprets packet control bytes as transmission unit info.

Socket private state stores source and destination or final addresses with flow label, destination cache cookie, reference counted transmit options, hop limit, path discovery mode, traffic class, address cache flags, multicast hops, fragment size, unicast and multicast output interfaces, a receive option union offering individual one bit flags or a combined sixteen bit view, source preference and minimum hop count, received flow info, sticky packet info, option and path message buffers, and multicast and anycast membership lists. A transmission control request wrapper embeds only a transmission control request structure.
Flag bit helpers map a symbolic suffix to a generic bit operation on socket internet flags for test, set, clear and assign.

Read and write mapping macros reference their mapping and offset arguments multiple times and introduce a local value temporary, so arguments with side effects would be evaluated repeatedly and only side effect free expressions are safe. Bulk helpers do not validate that offset plus length stays within the mapped extent.

Iteration advances shared iterator state even when callbacks partially consume, so callers must handle short progress and must not retry without accounting for already advanced offsets and counts. Header length computation warns once when the transport offset was never set, indicating wrong header setup order. Array iteration aborts on unexpected entry kinds rather than skipping them.

Mapping helpers perform no locking or atomicity. They are plain inline loads, stores and branches on caller owned objects and rely on external synchronization for concurrent access. Bitmap stub helpers likewise require no locking because they hold no state.
Each examined header defines a preprocessor guard macro that prevents multiple inclusion. The guard has no runtime behavior.
